Dev updates week 6 | 5.12.-12.12. We just finished up the meeting for today. Stand up calls will always be hosted at https://meet.ethereum.org/epf-standup Okay great - thanks Josh - apologies for missing the meeting today. I'll provide an update tomorrow then. No problem. Please add your desire to update to the GitHub Issue! Will do - I'll submit an update shortly 🙂 Any reason why someone would build empty blocks (or just incl. a few txs) as a validator? E.g. https://etherscan.io/block/16114268 https://etherscan.io/block/15786139 These don't seem to be related to MEV or censorship. Just an error? Then there's another category of blocks that only utilize <10% of block space. E.g. https://etherscan.io/block/16120136 https://etherscan.io/block/16120665 https://etherscan.io/block/16120598 I guess these are more likely related to MEV, or guaranteed tx ordering. Or would there be any other reasons? If anyone's interested, I created a Dune dashboard to track network utilization https://dune.com/wslyvh/network-utilization empty blocks could just be a bug or some issue w/ infra s.t. the validator could not get a more full execution payload in time the stock block building algo right after the merge was "start with an empty execution payload in case the validator needs it ASAP" and only extend the payload as the EL has time so you can start to see timing things crop up where this becomes an issue and with small numbers of transactions you could see a similar reason where the EL builder prioritizes "local" transactions vs those received from gossip (this is a distinction at least geth has) Got it. Just plain user/validator errors.. I guess I've been overthinking some of these things 😅 wouldn't "local" transactions still mean private deals? it could be other more sophisticated things but it can be hard to tell "local" here means that it was a transaction submitted directly via RPC to the node, which could in turn be gossiped as well geth just has some priority for packing those types of transactions into a block vs others For a while an EL was returning blocks with no transactions because they ran out of time to process i think... any block is better than no block in terms of the network health, so it's possible that at times things end up empty... Interesting. Thanks. Very helpful Any validator at home using an older version of geth (in fact I'm not sure if the fix was released) will be using very little gas https://twitter.com/vdWijden/status/1588463072251088896?s=19

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: empty blocks could just be a bug or some issue w/ infra s.t. the validator could not get a more full execution payload in time

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: the stock block building algo right after the merge was "start with an empty execution payload in case the validator needs it ASAP" and only extend the payload as the EL has time

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: so you can start to see timing things crop up where this becomes an issue

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: and with small numbers of transactions you could see a similar reason where the EL builder prioritizes "local" transactions vs those received from gossip (this is a distinction at least geth has)

excerpts.author: wslyvh
excerpts.content: Got it. Just plain user/validator errors.. I guess I've been overthinking some of these things 😅

excerpts.author: wslyvh
excerpts.content: wouldn't "local" transactions still mean private deals?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: it could be other more sophisticated things but it can be hard to tell

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: "local" here means that it was a transaction submitted directly via RPC to the node, which could in turn be gossiped as well

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: geth just has some priority for packing those types of transactions into a block vs others
